items.title: Fed's Musalem: US likely needs several rate hikes by spring to control inflation | MarketScreener
items.excerpt: Published on 11/17/2026 at 07:33 am EST - Modified on 11/17/2026 at 07:34 am EST ... WASHINGTON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The US Federal Reserve many need several rate hikes to bring high inflation under control and should act soon to ensure the problem doesn't get worse, St. Louis Fed president Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday. "The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve price stability in a timely manner," Musalem said, arguing that the current policy rate, in the 3.75% to 4% range, is as much as a percentage point below where it needs to be to return inflation to the Fed's 2% target. It is currently running above 3%, and Musalem said the most likely scenario is that it remains elevated unless the Fed acts. The Fed next meets on Dec. 8-9 and is expected to approve a quarter percentage point rate hike. Musalem is not a voter on interest rate policy this year. "Inflation is too high...Looking ahead, risks are skewed toward persistent above-target inflation," with current policy not acting as significant restraint on growth that continues above trend, Musalem said in remarks prepared for delivery to a Central Bank of Argentina conference in Buenos Aires. "Moving sooner, while inflation expectations are anchored, has a better chance of succeeding without adverse impact on the labor market or economic growth," he said.

items.title: Hammack Favors Gradual Fed Hikes, Cites Firms’ Growing Willingness to Raise Prices | EconoTimes
items.excerpt: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented from the Fed’s Oct. 28 decision to hold rates, favoring a quarter-point increase as she raised concerns about firms passing price rises to customers. In a Nov. 16 interview with Bloomberg Television, Hammack said businesses appeared increasingly inclined to shift higher prices to customers. She reiterated her preference for a gradual pace of interest-rate moves. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) kept its target range at 3.75% to 4.00%. The vote was 10-2; Fed Governor Lisa D. Cook also dissented, with both her and Hammack favoring a 0.25-percentage-point increase. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported that the seasonally adjusted Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% in October from the previous month, following a 0.6% increase in September. The index excluding food and energy advanced 0.3% in October, matching its monthly gains in August and September. The October release lacks the usual year-over-year changes for affected series because the BLS did not collect October 2025 data during a lapse in appropriations. The CPI is separate from the personal consumption expenditures price index, whose annual change the Fed uses to assess its longer-run 2% inflation goal.

items.title: Is the Inflation Shock Starting to Lose Momentum? | Investing.com India
items.excerpt: Published 17-11-2026, 06:07 pm Updated 17-11-2026, 06:08 pm There’s more to inflation than oil prices, but the recent pullback in crude suggests that the inflationary pressure tied to the Iran conflict may be starting to ease. Even if energy prices continue to move lower, it’s unclear how quickly that relief will filter through to broader inflation measures. Still, the growing possibility of such an outcome offers a measure of encouragement. Maybe, just maybe, a light at the end of the tunnel is beginning to come into view. **Let’s start with the U.S. oil benchmark, West Texas Intermediate (WTI), which is trading near its lowest level since August at around $86 a barrel.** A break lower from here would signal growing confidence that the market expects the Middle East supply shock to continue easing, at least relative to the worst days of the war. **That confidence remains fragile, of course. **In the blink of an eye, the U.S. or Iran could launch an attack that sends the optimists running for cover once again. It’s still premature to rule out that possibility, but the decline in oil prices suggests that optimism is gaining traction at the margin. The price of gasoline is also feeding expectations for eventual disinflation. The spot price recently fell to its lowest level since mid-March. **More importantly, there are signs that diesel prices have peaked. **As a key fuel for freight transportation and industrial activity, diesel exerts an outsized influence on costs across the economy. While the earlier surge in prices will continue to feed through to inflation in the near term, the recent downturn hints that the inflation shock is beginning to lose momentum. **The pushback is that we’ve been here before, several times since the first attack on Feb. 28.** It’s impossible to know whether we’re looking at another false dawn or a genuine inflection point in the inflation outlook. A key reason for caution is the unstable stalemate in the Middle East. ... **Another reason for caution on the near-term disinflation outlook is the recent acceleration in U.S. economic growth, which appears set to continue in the fourth quarter. **The Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow model estimates that output will rise at a 3.5% annualized pace in Q4. If correct, the pickup in growth that began in Q3 will continue, marking the strongest back-to-back quarters in more than a year. Stronger growth could keep inflation higher for longer by sustaining consumer demand and labor-market strength, limiting the economy’s ability to cool price pressures. That’s a meaningful concern with inflation still running well above the Fed’s 2% target, helping explain why markets expect another rate hike at next month’s FOMC meeting. Another round of policy tightening appears reasonable based on the Cleveland Fed’s nowcast for November consumer inflation, which projects the year-over-year CPI at the headline level will move close to 4% again. **Higher inflation can help set the stage for its own decline.** Rising prices squeeze household and business budgets, while higher interest rates increase borrowing costs. Together, those forces can cool demand, ease pressure on labor markets and supply chains, and ultimately slow the pace of price increases. For now, however, the odds of meaningful near-term relief on the inflation front appear low. Encouraging signs are beginning to emerge, particularly in energy markets, but it would be premature to declare victory. If oil and diesel prices resume their climb due to a new phase of conflict in the Middle East, the inflation outlook could deteriorate quickly.

items.title: Chicago Fed President: Persistent High Inflation Could Be ‘Painful to Try to Get Rid Of’
items.excerpt: Andrew Montequin | November 16, 2026, 6:14 pm Inflation has been above the Federal Reserve Bank’s target since February 2021. Those five and a half years have seen periods of progress and setbacks. But the direction inflation is headed now — with high prices expanding beyond temporary shocks from tariffs and the Iran war — is raising eyebrows. “At this moment, we’ve got to be very cognizant that we’re dancing on the edge of something that’s hard and potentially painful to get rid of,” said Austan Goolsbee, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago. ... The consumer price index for all items rose 0.4% in one month, according to data released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) last week. Last year’s government shutdown prevented the BLS from comparing prices to October 2025. But estimates place the annual inflation rate near 4%, double the Fed’s target. When higher-than-desired inflation sticks around that long, “it’s even more painful to try to get rid of,” Goolsbee said. “If people start taking for granted that inflation is going to be this high next year, the year after, et cetera, then they start factoring it into their decisions.” If the expectation of sustained inflation hangs over businesses’ decisions on topics like wage negotiations and cost planning, the central bank can have a harder time bringing inflation down. That doesn’t mean there hasn’t been progress in the past half decade. “There have been times when we were making progress, and I thought we were on the path back to 2%,” Goolsbee said. Goolsbee pointed to “negative shocks,” including tariffs and high prices of oil, that knocked prices off of this path. But he sees a different trend emerging now, where services not directly connected to these shocks are starting to see inflation. Goolsbee gave health insurance as an example of a service that’s seeing price spikes. “Health insurance inflation is not coming from tariffs, is not coming from oil prices, is not coming from any of the things that you could envision turning on a dime,” Goolsbee said. “Historically, things like health insurance, when they get ramped up they stay up and they keep rising.”

items.title: Democrats’ Peltola ahead as counting nears end in Alaska Senate race – US politics live | US news | The Guardian
items.excerpt: ## Alaska midterm race could be called on Wednesday as Peltola remains ahead of Republican incumbent Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog. The final Senate race of this year’s midterm elections could be resolved tomorrow if Alaska election officials run the state’s ranked choice voting system to determine the result. With 98% of ballots counted, Democratic challenger Mary Peltola is out in front with 49.98% of the vote. By contrast, incumbent Republican senator Dan S Sullivan has a 45.93% share, according to the latest Associated Press figures. In terms of actual voting numbers, Peltola is ahead by just over 11,000, with 141,637 compared to Sullivan’s 130,162. All eyes will be on Peltola to see if she can keep the pace to achieve 50% of the ballot, two weeks on from the election. If not, then voters’ second choice votes will be counted. items.title: Morning News Brief - The Center Voter
items.excerpt: ### TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 17, 2026 CENTER VOTER Nov 17, 2026 Federal Level Senate Confirms Domenico to Appeals Court in 51-46 Vote The Senate on Monday confirmed U.S. District Judge Daniel Domenico of Colorado to the 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals by a vote of 51 to 46. Reuters reported that the vote leaves just three other appeals court nominees to confirm as Republicans work to fill judicial vacancies before Democrats take control of the chamber in January. Colorado’s Democratic senators, Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper, voted against him. They had raised concerns about his broad view of the government’s immigration detention authority and his refusal to acknowledge President Trump’s loss in the 2020 election. Domenico will succeed Judge Timothy Tymkovich, for whom he once clerked. 1, 2 Senate Moves Permitting Bill Toward Final Passage Vote The Senate voted 70 to 27 on Monday to end debate on a substitute amendment to a bipartisan permitting reform bill, setting up a final Senate vote before the Thanksgiving recess. The amendment, sponsored by Sen. Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia, strengthens provisions dealing with energy-hungry data centers and tribal sovereignty. The bill would speed the construction of energy, mining and infrastructure projects while limiting environmental challenges under several federal laws. Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto of Nevada has threatened to oppose a final vote unless a section affecting historic preservation is removed. The measure would still need to pass the House. 3 Trump Says He Takes No Responsibility for Ground Stop President Trump said Monday that he takes no responsibility for last week’s four-hour nationwide ground stop that disrupted thousands of flights. “I don’t take any responsibility,” Trump told reporters, adding that Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and his team “acted incredibly.” The president said he worked from the Oval Office during the crisis and saw no reason to address the public himself. He again blamed prior administrations for outdated air traffic equipment and urged Congress to quickly approve more money for upgrades. Duffy has indicated he will ask for roughly $50 billion, and Democrats have questioned how existing funds are being spent. 4 Trump Departs for Asia, Says Kim May Join Summit President Trump departed Monday for a multi-day trip to Asia that begins in Manila and ends with the first-ever three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Before leaving, Trump told reporters that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un “may come” to Shenzhen but that the decision is “up to President Xi.” He also said he plans to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, although his officials had said Friday that the topic would be avoided. Trump added that he would like to see Jensen Huang reinstated as chief executive of Nvidia. 5 Foxx Requests Recount in Close North Carolina House Race Rep. Virginia Foxx of North Carolina said Monday that she has requested a recount in her reelection race, where she trails Democrat Chuck Hubbard by 331 votes. Unofficial totals show Hubbard with 139,770 votes and Foxx with 139,439, a margin within the 1 percent that state law allows for a recount. Foxx, an 11-term Republican, is the only Republican congressional candidate in the state to seek one. She said in a statement that she expects a smooth process that respects state law. The state elections board plans to finish a machine recount by Nov. 23 and to consider certification on Nov. 24. 6, 7 Van Hollen Says Bid to Replace Schumer Is Gaining Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said Monday that his challenge to Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer is gaining momentum. “Well, I’m the underdog, but we are really moving in the right direction here,” Van Hollen told NPR’s Morning Edition. He argued that Democratic leaders should stay out of contested primaries, pointing to incoming Sens. Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota. He also called for an end to further funding for the war in Iran. Schumer says he has enough votes to remain leader, and the winner will need close to 30 votes in a secret ballot. 8 Khanna Urges Democrats to Pass Iran War Refund Checks Rep. Ro Khanna of California called on Monday for Democrats to pass $1,700 refund checks for Americans during their first week in control of Congress in January. “The first week in January, the House and Senate must pass a $1,700 refund check to Americans,” Khanna said in a statement. He introduced the Illegal War Refund Act in September to offset higher fuel prices, food prices and other costs he links to the Iran war. The bill drew four co-sponsors and was referred to House committees without further action. Democrats will hold at least 256 House seats and 55 Senate seats in the new Congress. 9 ... Braun Launches Bid for Second Term as Indiana Governor Indiana Gov. Mike Braun announced Monday evening that he will seek reelection in 2028. The Republican made the announcement at a special event in Indianapolis. Braun credits his focus on affordability, including suspending the state gas tax for more than half of the year, with sheltering Indiana Republicans from this month’s national wave of Democratic victories. He will begin 2027 as the first Indiana governor since 2012 without a Republican supermajority in the state House. Attorney General Todd Rokita and Lt. Gov. Micah Beckwith, both Republicans, are seen as possible primary challengers, according to WTHR.

items.excerpt: Marvin Sapp on new album, viral 'close the doors' backlash and gospel's Super Bowl ambitions LOS ANGELES (AP) — Marvin Sapp is focusing on life after internet backlash with his new album, “Restoration.” The gospel singer faced criticism after a video showed him telling ushers to “close the doors” during a church offering. Released Friday, the album reflects on grace and recovery from public judgment. Sapp recently signed with Roc Nation Distribution, maintaining ownership of his music. Despite criticism, he insists his sound remains Christ-centered. Sapp remarried this year, finding support in his new wife, LaBoris Cole-Sapp. Looking ahead, he believes gospel could headline a Super Bowl halftime show, with Kirk Franklin leading the charge. ... Grammy nominations snub Harry Styles and hip-hop, while surprises include Dolly Parton NEW YORK (AP) — The 2027 Grammy Award nominees have been announced, sparking inevitable discussions about snubs and surprises. Notably, there's no hip-hop in most general field categories, a shift from last year. Women dominate many major categories, with only Bruno Mars breaking the trend. Harry Styles did not receive a nomination and Noah Kahan only received one. Beyoncé makes history with her 100th career nomination. Dolly Parton and Tim Curry receive posthumous nominations. A new category for Asian pop music performance has been introduced, but BTS chose not to participate and thus wasn't nominated. The awards will air on Feb. 7. ... LOS ANGELES (AP) — Glenn Close has finally received her first Oscar, an honorary award at the Governors Awards in Los Angeles. Close, 79, was honored alongside director Ridley Scott, animator Floyd Norman, and producers Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler. Close, who has been nominated eight times without a win, expressed deep gratitude for the recognition.

items.excerpt: ## 1. Six Nigerians on the 2027 Grammy list ### What happened The Recording Academy announced nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards on Monday. Nigerian acts hold four of the five spots in Best African Music Performance: Asake twice, for Gratitude and for Jogodo with Wizkid, Tems for Big Daddy, and Ayra Starr with Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo for Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?). The fifth nominee is Ghana’s King Ayisoba with Rocky Dawuni. Three Nigerian albums are up for Best Global Music Album: Tems’ Love Is a Kingdom, Davido’s Oriadé and Ayra Starr’s Starrgirl. Burna Boy is nominated in Best Global Music Performance for Dai Dai, his World Cup song with Shakira. Tems also picked up R&B recognition for What You Need. Outlets count her total differently, with some listing three nominations and others four, because she appears as a songwriter in Best R&B Song as well as a performer. ### Why it matters Nigerian artists are now competing with each other for the same trophy, which says a lot about how far the sound has travelled. The ceremony is on 7 February 2027 at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and will air on ABC and stream on Disney+ and Hulu. For background, see our ranking of the best Afrobeats albums of 2026. Source: ThisDay; TVC News; Peoples Gazette. ## 2. AMAA 2026: Kenya and Côte d’Ivoire lead, Nigeria picks up key prizes ### What happened The 22nd Africa Movie Academy Awards held on Sunday night at the Marriott Hotel in Ikeja, Lagos. One Woman One Bra, a Kenya-Nigeria co-production directed by Vincho Nchogu, won Best Film, Best Film in an African Language and Best Debut Feature. The Colour of Exile from Côte d’Ivoire won the most awards, four, including Best Director and Best Actress for Naky Sy Savane. Nigeria’s main winners were Wale Ojo (Best Actor, Lights Out), Linda Ejiofor (Best Supporting Actress, The Herd) and To Adaego With Love, which took Best Nigerian Film and the screenplay award. The Herd also won for production design and make-up, The Creek for visual effects, and Evi for soundtrack. ### Why it matters Nollywood still dominated the nomination lists, but the top prizes went elsewhere this year, a reminder that the rest of the continent’s film industry is growing fast too. Source: Channels TV; TheCable Lifestyle; Afrocritik. ## 3. Box office: Five Figurines on top, Agbara Nla keeps climbing ### Five Figurines and Issakaba Returns Akay Mason’s thriller Five Figurines, starring Bimbo Akintola and Odunlade Adekola, opened at number one over the 13 to 15 November weekend. Its distributors put the takings at more than ₦64.8 million and called it the biggest November opening for a Nollywood film. Industry tracker Fusion Intelligence reports about ₦64.4 million from 9,789 admissions, around 30 per cent of the weekend’s total, with Sunday alone bringing in ₦33.1 million. Issakaba Returns opened second with ₦44 million, or ₦46.5 million including previews. ### Agbara Nla: The Return passes ₦513 million Distributor Nile Entertainment said on Monday that the remake of Mike Bamiloye’s 1993 Christian classic has now made more than ₦513.4 million since it opened on 1 October. That makes it the second-biggest Nollywood film of 2026 behind Call of My Life, and the ninth-biggest Nollywood title ever. ... ## 4. Olamide drops Time and Space ### What happened Olamide released Time and Space on Monday through YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. It has 10 songs and runs about 32 minutes. FOLA is the only guest, on Jaiye, and October’s single Burukutu sits at track four. Olamide said he painted the cover art himself. The album follows his self-titled 2025 record, Olamidé, which had a much longer guest list.
